rationales.1: Invoicing for trades priced like a day rate, plus a subhead describing the photo-to-invoice flow and a line naming sole traders, answers what and for whom entirely inside the first screenful.
rationales.2: The four-hour figure is carefully downgraded to an early signal from eleven pilot users, though the ninety-eight percent claim stands as a bare fact with no stated basis.
rationales.3: Pricing is transparent with the VAT note and an honest no-card promise, but the only button on the page is see-the-rate-card and the trial itself never gets an unmistakable CTA, only a bold text line.
rationales.4: Day-rate pricing, no subscription games, and a when-it-goes-wrong section speak directly to a subscription-skeptic tradesperson in plain language on a clean phone layout.
rationales.5: Competent conventional craft with a limited palette and steady rhythm, though the dark mode drifts between peach labels and mint accents and the desktop leaves large unused right-hand space.
rationales.6: The beta is labeled still-in-testing, the estimate is explicitly not a promise, and this is the only candidate that labels the testimonial as a fictional persona rather than presenting it as real.
rationales.7: Priced-like-a-day-rate is a good sentence, but the page asserts it inside an otherwise generic marketing structure rather than demonstrating it through form.
rationales.8: Mechanics are entirely conventional with no real break attempted, which respects the budget while spending none of it.
rationales.9: No enterprise tier hiding behind a sales call and the evening quote not waiting on a chatbot are distinctive, though the overall frame reads closer to standard candid-SaaS register.
rationales.10: The page scans quickly and stays unperformative, but the price a skeptic came for sits five sections deep behind stats and features.
